summary.text: Ritesh Tandon, an engineer and business executive, lost the November 3, 2026 election for California's 17th Congressional District to Ro Khanna.
He was the Republican candidate in the district in 2020 and 2022, finishing second to Khanna in both general elections, and ran in the 2024 primary as a Democrat.
He was the lead plaintiff in Tandon v. Newsom, a 2021 U.S. Supreme Court case on COVID-19 restrictions on religious gatherings.

paragraphs.text: Tandon describes himself as having come to the United States from India at age 28 and as a Silicon Valley resident for two decades, according to his Ballotpedia survey.
He earned a B.S. in mechanical engineering from L.D. College of Engineering in India, and an M.S. in computer engineering and an M.B.A. from Santa Clara University.

He worked on unified communications products at Cisco, starting in engineering and moving into technical marketing, and later managed global strategic alliances at Jabra, according to his 2022 survey; his 2026 survey says he spent 24 years in the tech industry before founding his own company.
He is CEO of Kricel Corporation and a research fellow at UC Berkeley's Haas School of Business.
Tandon has served as chief liaison officer for the Smart Village Movement, as vice-chairman of UPMA, and on the executive committee of the Sankara Eye Foundation.

He was the first-named applicant in Tandon v. Newsom, in which the U.S. Supreme Court on April 9, 2021 granted an injunction against California limits on at-home religious gatherings over four dissents. His 2026 survey describes the 5-4 decision as a win for the right to worship.

As the Republican nominee he ran against Khanna in the 2020 general election (28.7%) and the 2022 general election (29.1%). In the March 2024 primary he appeared on the ballot as a Democrat and received 4.9%, not advancing.
His 2026 Ballotpedia survey described affordability, public safety and education as priorities.
He received 28.2% of the vote to Ro Khanna's 71.8%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
